EU 3D Printing Import & Landed Cost Calculator

Another tool I built because I needed it myself

Sticker prices on foreign webshops no longer tell the whole story. Since 1 July 2026 the EU charges a €3 customs duty per item on parcels valued up to €150, and import VAT applies to the item price, shipping, and duty combined. Enter what you are buying, how many distinct product categories are in the box, and your country's VAT rate — the calculator gives you the full landed cost in EUR instantly. Built for EU makers ordering filaments, nozzles, heater blocks, and printer parts from outside the EU. Runs entirely in your browser — no uploads, no accounts, no cookies.

Features

€3 flat customs duty per item category
Import VAT for all 27 EU member states
Correct VAT base: item + shipping + duty
Over-€150 orders with custom duty rate
Instant landed-cost breakdown in EUR
No account, no cookies — nothing uploaded

Disclaimer: This is an estimate

This calculator is a planning aid, not legal or tax advice. The €3 duty and VAT rules follow Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382 as of 1 July 2026, but rates, thresholds, and your country's VAT can change. In practice the duty is collected from the seller, platform, or carrier rather than charged to you at the door — but it still shapes the price you pay. The upcoming EU handling fee (expected no later than 1 November 2026) is not included, and IOSS sellers may fold VAT into the checkout price. Always confirm the final number with the seller.

Direct answer

What does that order really cost delivered?

Add the item price, the shipping, and the customs duty — €3 per distinct item category on parcels up to €150 since 1 July 2026 — then apply your country's VAT to that whole base. A €24.99 spool with €4.99 shipping costs €29.98 before duty; add €3.00 and the VAT base is €32.98. At 21% VAT that is €6.93, for a landed total of €39.91. Calculating VAT on the sticker price alone is the classic mistake — shipping and duty are both taxable.

EU handling fee (separate)Amount TBA — expected €2–€4 per parcelExpected 1 Nov 2026 · not included here

The €3 is charged per item line by tariff classification, not per parcel — one box with two different product types draws €6. Quantity within one type does not multiply it.

Import VAT is due at the standard rate of the member state where the goods are consumed. Reduced rates exist for some goods but not for printer filament and hardware — and rates change, so confirm yours on large orders.

How to compare an import order honestly

  1. 1

    Take the sticker price and shipping from checkout

    Use the goods value before shipping — that is what customs values the consignment on. Add the international shipping line exactly as the shop quotes it, because shipping is part of the VAT base.

  2. 2

    Count distinct product categories in the box

    Same filament in three colours is one tariff line — one €3 duty. Add a heater block or a PTFE tube of a different classification and it becomes two categories, €6. Enter that number, not the number of items.

  3. 3

    Pick your country and compare the landed total

    The landed price is the number to hold against an EU-based shop. If the gap is thin, buying locally usually wins on shipping time, returns, and support — and you avoid the courier's own handling fee on top.

EU Import Cost FAQ

Why is there an extra €3 fee on my 3D printing parts order from outside the EU?

Under EU customs regulations, the previous low-value exemption threshold was replaced by a flat €3 customs duty per distinct product category on parcels valued under €150. The €150 duty-free allowance was abolished on 1 July 2026, and the flat €3 rate applies per item line — based on tariff classification — until 1 July 2028, when normal customs tariff rates return.

How is import VAT calculated on international 3D printer parts?

EU import VAT is calculated on the cumulative total of your item price, shipping costs, and the applied customs duty combined. At 21% VAT, a €24.99 spool with €4.99 shipping and €3.00 duty is taxed on €32.98 — that is €6.93 of VAT, not €5.25. Calculating VAT on the goods price alone is the most common mistake people make when estimating an import.

Does the €3 customs duty apply per spool or per parcel?

Per item line, not per parcel and not per quantity. Three spools of the same PLA share one tariff classification, so they count as one category and one €3 duty. Add a heater block to the same order and it is classified separately — two categories, €6 of duty. That is why the calculator asks for the number of distinct product categories rather than the number of items.

Do I pay the customs duty myself at the door?

Usually not directly. The €3 duty is collected from the seller, platform, or carrier involved in the sale and transport — customers are generally spared an extra payment at delivery. In practice the cost is typically folded into the price you already paid. The duty exists either way, so it belongs in your cost comparison between EU and non-EU shops.

Which VAT rate applies to my order?

Import VAT is charged at the standard rate of the member state where the goods are consumed — from 17% in Luxembourg to 27% in Hungary. The dropdown covers all 27 EU countries. Rates change, so if you are comparing large orders, confirm your country's current standard rate before committing.

What about the extra handling fee couriers keep mentioning?

A separate EU handling fee on e-commerce parcels is expected no later than 1 November 2026, with the exact amount still to be set by delegated act — industry estimates put it between €2 and €4 per parcel. It is a fee, not a customs duty, and this calculator does not include it yet. Treat the result here as the cost before that fee lands.
